newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch TV football contract 'too long' -Van Miert.
newsitem.headline: Dutch TV football contract 'too long' -Van Miert.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Thursday that a plan by the Dutch football association KNVB to grant seven years of exclusive broadcasting to a sports channel in which it is a shareholder was too long.

"Seven years is too long," Van Miert told the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary affairs committee. He hinted that the commission might ask KNVB to reduce the period to five years -- as was decided for a similar case involving British TV channel BSkyB.
KNVB notified the commission in August of its plan to grant a channel called Sports 7 exclusive rights to broadcast Dutch premier league football matches.
There is no deadline for the Commission to come to a decision on the matter, but it usually informs companies of its preliminary findings within two months of notification.
Other shareholders in Sports 7 include Philips Electronics NV, ING NV, Endemol, NUON, Koninklijke PTT, Stichting Kabelbelangen and De Telegraaf.
Van Miert said that when assessing the case the Commission would make a distinction between regular sports events and exceptional ones such as the Olympic Games.
